title: An fppf covering has a locally quasi-finite flat refinement
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be a small fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]. There exist a small family of morphisms $g_j:T_j\to S$ which is jointly surjective, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], together with indices $i(j)\in I$ and $S$-morphisms $T_j\to S_{i(j)}$ whose composites with $S_{i(j)}\to S$ equal $g_j$. Empty schemes and empty indexing families are allowed.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, take the empty indexing family; all requested assertions are vacuous. Otherwise, joint surjectivity of the given fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site] says that for every point $s\in S$ there are an index $i(s)\in I$ and a point $x_s\in S_{i(s)}$ mapping to $s$. Choose these data for all $s$; the point-indexed family is small in the fixed universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. If $I=\varnothing$, the same joint-surjectivity condition forces $S=\varnothing$, already covered.

proof.text: For each chosen pair $(s,x_s)$ over $S_{i(s)}$, apply [lem-trf-fppf-local-qf-neighbourhood] to the flat locally finitely presented morphism $S_{i(s)}\to S$ and the image point $s$. It gives a scheme $T_s$, a map $T_s\to S_{i(s)}$, and a structural map $g_s:T_s\to S$ whose composite is the original map, with $s\in g_s(T_s)$ and $g_s$ flat, locally of finite presentation, and locally quasi-finite. The family $(g_s)_{s\in S}$ is jointly surjective because its member indexed by $s$ contains $s$ in its image, and each member factors through the original covering member $S_{i(s)}\to S$. Thus it is the required small refinement.
